newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS-Norway's Fokus bank seeks merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Norway's Fokus bank seeks merger.

text.p: Norway's fourth largest bank, Fokus Bank ASA, said on Tuesday it had proposed a merger with Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank), a niche institution specialising in mortgage loans.
The move was the latest attempt at restructuring Norway's crowded banking scene.
Fokus proposed an exchange ratio of 3.3 shares in Fokus Bank for each share in BNbank, with 20 percent of the consideration paid in cash.

Based on Fokus' closing share price on Monday of 58.50 crowns on the Oslo Bourse, the exchange ratio equals a price on BNbank of 179.85 crowns per share and 10 crowns in dividend, Fokus said in a statement.
A BNbank official had no immediate comment on the merger proposal and said it would take a few weeks before the board could offer a recommendation to shareholders.
The market reacted quicker with BNbank up 24 crowns at 191 crowns in morning trade on Tuesday. Fokus gained a crown to trade at 59.50 crowns.

Fokus's business is 90 percent based on the western side of Norway with the remainder in Oslo. Analysts see growth potential coming from the booming Norwegian economy, gains in market share from smaller competitors and continued cost-cutting.

"While Fokus represents a supplement for BNbank, the smaller bank would not supplement the business of Fokus," one Oslo-based analyst said. "Maybe Fokus believes they can get so much synergy out of this that it will pay off."
"Another possible explanation is that a merger would act as a poison pill for other banks. Fokus would grow bigger, making it more difficult to be taken over," he said.

The joint bank would have total assets of about 60 billion crowns ($8.8 billion), including BNbank's 24 billion. With BNbank, Fokus would confirm its position as fourth largest bank in Norway. It is also the third largest commercial bank.
Fokus, which is the fruit of mergers between seven banks between 1987 and 1991, said it expected to save 80 million crowns in four years through synergy.
Both banks are headquartered in Trondheim and Fokus said the city would remain base for the merged unit, with BNbank becoming a subsidiary.
Fokus last month said 1996 net profits rose 7.7 percent to 462 million crowns from a year earlier thanks to successful regional banking which emphasizes local expertise and decentralised authorities.
BNbank's 1996 net profits rose to 127 million crowns from 95 million a year earlier. ($ = 6.852 Norwegian Crowns)
